Brother Corcoran read the report on the Diamond,* which was

It was moved by Brother Corcoran that it be the sense of this

ANNUAL COMMUNICATION FROM THE EXECUTIVE COUNCIL
TO THE 1923 CONVENTION OF THE PSI UPSILON
FRATERNITY

At this convention in the Ninetieth Year of our Fraternity,
the Executive Council extends its congratulations and felicitations
to the chapters upon their preservation of the high ideals and ex

cellent personnel of our Fraternity. The reports received from the
various members of the Council who have visited different chapters
over the past year are most gratifying and show the Fraternity to
be in a prosperous condition.

Organization: Last year in the Annual Communication to the
Convention the Council set forth quite clearly the fact that our

present form of organization is satisfactory and cautioned the
Fraternity not to become too involved in its procedure.

Although, as set forth in that Communication, Psi Upsilon is a
society of the spirit more than the form, yet the Council feels that
we must not let our regard for traditions make us unwilling to ask

ourselves if we are fully meeting the evident challenge of the new
order of the day. Are we to remain static or are we to be conserva
tively constructive in our procedure as a Fraternity?

There is a wide difference between the reactionary and con

servative attitude of mind in reference to our fraternal activities.
The reactionary mind is the onethat will not question, that does
not want to know if Psi U is meeting its real obligations; the con
servative mind, opposed to radicalism, is the one that would con
scientiously question, that does want to know if we are doing all
that the Fraternity might do for its members. Surely there is
reason for us at all times to ask ourselves this question, letting our
action wait upon the answer.

Therefore, your Executive Council would suggest to you the
appointing by the Executive Council of a committee to consider
this broad question of our policy and procedure in reference to our
Organization itself as regards reports and records, in reference to
the very vital question of scholarship, in reference to a permanent

12

endowment fund, and such other matters which should be rather
clearly set forth as a guide for our Fraternity through the coming
years. Such a committee is merely to investigate and report its
findings and recommendations in writing, through the Council, to
the chapters not later than March 1st, 11)24, for consideration at
the Annual Convention of 1924.

Records: The compiling of facts for the supplement to the
general catalog has demonstrated that some of the chapters are be
coming rather careless as regards their records, and so, in the
recommendations which the Council makes for the above
general
committee, it is felt that some arrangement should be made by
which the Fraternity should be certair^ every year that the records
of each chapter are in good form. There should be an alumnus
master of the rolls ancJ two undergraduates for each chapter.
Scholarship: While, in our last communication, the Council
set forth the necessity for raising the standard of scholarship, we

would again emphasize and hope that the committee will devise
ways and means by which this may be obtained. The scholarship
standing of Psi U in the various institutions where we have chap
ters is none too gratifying and something must be done to place

every chapter of Psi U among the upper half in scholarship ranking.
Permanent Endowment Fund: Although the Council has ap

pointed a committee to investigate and report on the question of a
permanent endowment fund in conformance with the vote of the
last convention, it is hoped that this question of endowment may
be incorporated in the general survey and recommendations to the

Fraternity.
Songs: The Council would urge the Convention to recommend

back to the chapters for their serious consideration, the proper sing
ing of our songs. Our Song Committee has worked diligently on

the revision of the songs and feels, together with the Council and
a large portion of the alumni, that there is no better way to pre

serve the spirit of Psi U than by the proper singing of songs dur
ing the undergraduate years in order that they may be correctly
taken away in the memories and act as a golden tie through the

years to come with the undergraduate years gone by.

13

Diamond: The Council would recommend that the Fraternity

give serious consideration to the further support of the Diamond
and that a special committee be appointed at this Convention to
consider the report of the Diamond and recommend back to this
Convention ways and means of giving it further support and making
it permanent. Those who have been conducting its affairs certainly
deserve a vote of deep appreciation from the Fraternity and should
be relieved, in a degree, at least, of their burdening duties.

Election to Council: The Council would call attention to the
fact that the terms of Brothers Austin M. Poole, Delta '87 and Ed
ward L. Stevens, Ghi '9&, expire at this Convention and that Brother
Luke I. Wilson, Mu '95, has found it necessary to resign. There
fore, it will be necessary lor the Convention to elect three new

members to the Executive Council.

Necrology: Since The Diamond is reporting, in so far as pos
sible, the deaths ol all Psi U's, the Council feels that this method
is much more prompt than the annual notification in its communi
cation; therelore the list ol our deceased brothers during the past
year is omitted, but the regret of the Council that any of our

brothers have passed on is none the less marked.

Conduct at Conventions: In view ol the restrictions as set
forth by the Constitution of the United States supplemented by the
Volstead Act, and the regulations as enforced by local authorities,
the Council would not only urge, but, in so far as lies within its
power, would insistthat all brothers, both undergraduates and
alumni, at any convention, refrain from the use in any way what
soever of intoxicating liquors. It must be remembered that any
indiscretion reflects not only on the Fraternity but especially on

the chapter where the convention is being held.

Graduation; The attached table shows the relative standing
of the active classes of each chapter of the Fraternity.
The Council regrets that in many instances chapters show a
decided falling off in the delegations between freshmen and senior
years, not so much due apparently to low scholarship as to leaving
the college or university to enter business.

14

Again the Council would emphasize that a chapter can best be
judged by the size and standing of its senior delegation and that
no man, no matter how good he may be, should be initiated into
Psi Upsilon unless there is a reasonable assurance of his gradua
tion. Four years is all too short for a man to be imbued with the

spirit and the tradition of Psi Upsilon and he can reflect no better
credit upon the Fraternity than to graduate with his delegation
with scholastic honors.

Respectfully and fraternally submitted,
EXECUTIVE COUNCIL,
E. H. Nayloe,

Secretary-Recorder.
Approved May 8th, 1928.;

REPORT TO THE 1923 CONVENTION OF PSI UPSILON

The Board of Editors ol The Diamond herewith submits to you
the report of its stewardship for the year ending May 1st, 1923.

Since the last convention we have published four issues at the
regular intervals and the June numlier ol this year will go to press
on May 29th next.
To-date in this college year we have called for but 50% of the

chapters guarantee fund as established at the last convention, but
we find that it will be necessary to call upon the several chapters
for an additional 15% on June 1st bringing the final total to 65%
which is the same as last year. A complete financial report is
attached.
We have endeavored to maintain the same high standard with
which we started when The Diamond was revived three years ago
and we modestly think that the publication is one of which the
fraternity may be proud. We have had many letters from alumni
and chapters complimenting us on the several issues and we assure

you that as long as we are entrusted with this work we will try to
live up to your expectations.

The subscriptions have not been followed up by the chapters
this year as in the first two years and of course The Diamond work
ing force has not the time nor has the magazine the funds with
which to carry on this phase of our work. It is regrettable to note

that the number of paid subscriptions hasi fallen off, somewhat and
largely due to the neglect of our busy alumni to write a; check and
mail it in. Your earnest co-operation in regard to subscription is

urgently requested.
More particularly, it has been somewhat discouraging to note

the almost total lack of new subscriptions from the brothers gradu
ating or otherwise leaving the several chapters. The Zeta chapter
is the only pointed exception and there we understand it is re

quired of all seniors to subscribe for five years. In the other chap
ters the lack of this is doubtless due purely to oversight.
Your Board of Editors had hoped that the national endowment
fund of the fraternity might become a reality at this convention

REPORT OF THE TREASURER

By virtue of Resolution No. 11 passed at the last Convention,
your Treasurer was enabled to make a reduction of 40% on the
annual tax on the Chapters for 1923.
In the accompanying balance sheet setting forth the Treas
urer's report as of May 1st, 19i23, are listed as taxes receivable
(unpaid), the following:

Beta 1'922 $250 OO.

Theta 1923 69,00
Beta 192S 153,00
Beta Beta 1923 54,00

Total $526.00

Since the compilation of this balance sheet the last three items
have been paid in full. In other words, Theta, Beta and Beta Beta
taxes lor 1923 have been duly paid and credited. In addition $80,00
has since been paid, applying on the Beta taxes lor 1922, leaving a

balance of 170.00, representing an amount assessed on 34 seniors at
the Beta Chapter last year, at the then rate ol $5.00 per capita.

Resolution No. 12 passed by the last year's convention, and now
effective, provided lor the elimination ol tax on members of the
senior class at the Beta for reasons considered justifiable by the
Convention as representing the Chapters, and in which reasons the
Executive Council unofficially concurs.

In the adoption of this report, the Treasurer recommends that
Resolution No. 12 referred to, be considered retroactive as apply
ing to the members of the senior class ol last year (1922), as they
assumedly were in college when the Resolution was passed and cur
rently subject to the effect ol the Resolution, although taxes were
actually due just prior to its passage. This action will balance the
accounts ol the Beta Chapter and leave no outstanding items on the
books ol the Treasurer.
